newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA GUIDES SRI LANKA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA GUIDES SRI LANKA TO VICTORY.

text.p: A superb all-round performance by Sanath Jayasuriya helped Sri Lanka to a 75-run victory over Pakistan in a low-scoring Singer Champions' Trophy match on Friday.

The elegant opener, who was instrumental in his country's World Cup victory earlier this year, stroked 33 off 34 balls and then cleaned up Pakistan's lower order, finishing with three for 15 from five overs.
Sri Lanka, defending a modest total of 206, never looked back after capturing four early wickets, dismissing Wasim Akram's side for 131 in 36 overs.
Medium-pacer Sajeeva de Silva, who finished with three for 48, made the early breakthroughs removing openers Saeed Anwar and Shahid Afridi with just 29 runs on the board.
Ijaz Ahmed offered some lone resistance before he was run out for 49 when he tried to increase the tempo.
Akram blamed his frontline batsmen for what he called their "unprofessional approach". The score, he said, was not beyond the team's reach, but "we made a mess of things".
Sri Lanka's captain Arjunga Ranatunga said: "We bowled brilliantly and fielded well to defend the total. It's not easy to score on the wicket."
Sri Lanka, however, suffered a blow when Kumara Dharmasena injured his shoulder while trying to field a catch and was unable to bowl. He was later taken to hospital for X-rays.
Earlier, Akram led from the front with a fine exhibition of swing bowling to restrict Sri Lanka to a modest score.
The Pakistam skipper took four for 42 as the normally fluent Sri Lanka batsmen struggled to score.
Middle-order batsman Roshan Mahanama top scored with 37 in 54 balls, while number three Asanka Gurusinha grafted 31 from 73 balls as Sri Lanka were bowled out in 49.3 overs.
